title: Riot Games World Championship — Paris
tagline: One stage, two launches: Riot's new virtual band True Damage and a Louis Vuitton partnership.

body: This ceremony had to carry several major brand priorities in a single performance: the global debut of Riot's new virtual music group True Damage, a high-profile partnership with Louis Vuitton, and the celebration of the League of Legends World Championship, the pinnacle event in global esports.

Riot's opening ceremonies had become synonymous with spectacle, so fans expected to be surprised. The challenge was to push further creatively — and make the moment feel just as special in the arena as it did for the millions watching at home.

I led the creative and technical execution end to end, from concept development through live performance — directing a multidisciplinary team across design, animation, choreography and live production, presenting to stakeholders, and managing internal teams and external partners throughout.

Every element — stage and lighting design, hologram content and choreography — was aligned with Riot's business goals: launch True Damage as a band fans would want to follow, and give the Louis Vuitton partnership a moment worthy of both brands. On site, I made the real-time calls that kept the show flawless and on-brand.
led: Aligned stage, lighting, holograms and choreography with Riot's launch goals
Managed internal teams and external partners on site

impact.note: The opening ceremony earned Riot Games its second Emmy Award and reached more than 100 million viewers — then took over social with 1.1B+ impressions, a 104% increase in Twitter video views and a 221% surge in Instagram Story engagement.
